summary: Adds a search endpoint, a hardcoded payment key and a pagination change. It also loosens the Dockerfile, the deploy script and the CI workflow, and downgrades lodash.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.problem: The search_items handler puts the q request parameter straight into the SQL text with an f-string.
findings.consequence: Any caller of /search can inject SQL and read or change any data in items.db.
findings.fix: Pass q to cur.execute as a bound parameter.
findings.suggested_change: cur.execute("SELECT id, name, price FROM items WHERE name = ?", (q,))

findings.title: Pagination skips the first page
findings.problem: The list_items handler now computes the offset as page times PAGE_SIZE. Page 1 therefore starts at row 20.
findings.consequence: Clients never see the first 20 items, and every page is shifted by one.
findings.fix: Restore the offset to page minus one times PAGE_SIZE.

findings.title: Payment API key committed to source
findings.problem: The new config module hardcodes a Stripe key in the repository.
findings.consequence: Anyone with repository access can use the key against the payment account.
findings.fix: Revoke the key and load it from an environment variable or secret store.

findings.title: Pull request title interpolated into shell
findings.problem: The new step expands the pull request title directly inside the run script. A crafted title becomes shell commands.
findings.consequence: Any pull request author can run arbitrary commands on the CI runner.
findings.fix: Pass the title through an env variable and quote that variable in the script.

findings.title: lodash downgraded to a vulnerable release
findings.problem: The change pins lodash back from 4.18.1 to 4.17.15. That release has known command injection and prototype pollution flaws.
findings.consequence: Front-end code that uses lodash becomes exposed to these known flaws again.
findings.fix: Keep lodash at 4.18.1 or later in package.json and package-lock.json.

findings.title: Container now runs as root
findings.problem: The change removes the app user and the USER 10001 line. The Flask server now runs as root.
findings.consequence: Any code execution bug in the app, such as the new SQL injection, gains root inside the container.
findings.fix: Restore the useradd step and the USER 10001 line before EXPOSE.

findings.title: Base image no longer pinned
findings.problem: The change replaces the pinned python 3.12.7 slim image with python:latest.
findings.consequence: Builds can silently switch Python versions and break the app without any code change.
findings.fix: Pin the base image to a specific release tag again.

findings.title: Unquoted path in rm -rf
findings.problem: The deploy script now passes DEPLOY_DIR to rm -rf without quotes. The shell splits and globs the path.
findings.consequence: A DEPLOY_DIR value with spaces or glob characters makes the script delete the wrong paths.
findings.fix: Quote the variable and keep the non-empty guard.

findings.title: Deploy loop parses ls output
findings.problem: The loop now iterates over unquoted ls output instead of a glob. It prints bare names and splits names on whitespace.
findings.consequence: The deploy log shows wrong entries for any file name with spaces.
findings.fix: Restore the glob loop over the deploy directory.

findings.title: Changed endpoints have no tests
findings.problem: The repository has no tests for the new search endpoint or the changed pagination in list_items.
findings.consequence: Regressions like the pagination offset bug reach users without any automated check catching them.
findings.fix: Add tests for /search and for the first page of /items.
